transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you, and thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, well... I'm a little embarrassed to even say it, to be honest. I know I'm probably just overtired from my job, but... I came in because I've been having this little issue at home. Lately, when I'm in my little studio, and the house is completely quiet with nobody else around... I keep hearing voices. 

It's just, um, it's as clear as somebody standing right there in the room with me. They say my name, and they keep telling me that my work is being judged. And I know nobody is actually there, I really do. I just... I hope that doesn't sound too terrible? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to tell you about it. Am I explaining that okay?
How long have you been experiencing these voices?

Oh, um... well, I really hope you aren't upset with me for not coming in sooner. I just... I kept hoping it would just go away on its own, you know? But, um, I guess it's been about nine months now. Give or take? 

That's when the voices started, and also when I started getting this... this really silly fear that my work is being watched all the time. I know it's probably just my imagination running away with me, but that feeling has just been stuck in my head for those nine months. 

Is... is nine months a really bad amount of time to wait before seeing a doctor? I just didn't want to be a bother to anyone, or make a big fuss over nothing. I hope you understand?

Aside from the voices and the feeling that you are being watched, have you noticed any significant changes in your ability to take care of your daily hygiene or your motivation to perform your usual tasks?

Oh, um... well... I really try my best to keep up with everything, I promise I do. I don't want you to think I'm just letting myself go completely. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... sometimes, when I'm not all wound up and running around, I get a little... well, I don't know if lazy is the right word, but I just sort of stop. I can sit in my chair for hours and just let my coffee get completely cold right in front of me. I won't even answer my phone when people call, and... I haven't been going to my walking club either. I don't even care to pick up my paintbrush, which is silly because I usually love my painting so much. 

I just... I know I should be doing better, and I feel terrible admitting that I've been slacking off like that. I hope that doesn't make me sound awful? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
When you are speaking to others, do they ever tell you that your sentences are difficult to follow or that what you are saying doesn't seem to make sense?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really hope I haven't been confusing you today? 

I always try very hard to be clear when I talk to people, especially my clients at work. I know how important it is to communicate well. Nobody has ever mentioned that I don't make sense, or at least, they haven't said it to my face. 

Sometimes I might ramble a little bit if I'm nervous, like right now, maybe? But I always try to make sure my sentences go together the right way. Am I... am I making sense to you right now? I really want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.
Do you ever have any unusual beliefs, such as feeling that you have special powers or that ordinary events around you have a hidden, personal meaning specifically for you?

Oh, um... well, I don't know if "special powers" is the right word. I certainly don't think I'm anyone special, I promise. I'm just a regular person trying to do my job. 

But... I did get this idea stuck in my head, and I know it sounds a little silly now, so please don't think I'm completely crazy. I just... I started feeling like the other home-care agency in town, and maybe even some people down at the library, were... well, watching me. 

Not in a good way, either. I felt like they were looking at my paintings, and even my client papers, trying to steal some kind of opportunity that was meant for me. I know it sounds paranoid, and my friends told me it didn't make any sense at all, but... I just couldn't shake the feeling that I *knew* they were doing it. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound terrible or suspicious. I just couldn't help feeling that way. Is it... is it okay that I felt like that? I'm really trying to be honest with you.

You mentioned that these experiences have been going on for about nine months; during that entire nine-month period, have you consistently felt this lack of motivation and difficulty with your daily activities?

Oh, um... well, no, not the whole time. I really don't want you to think I've just been sitting around doing nothing for nine months straight! I always try to keep busy when I can. 

Actually, for a lot of that time... well, I was kind of the opposite. I was so wound up, you know? I had all these big plans, and I was just going and going. I hardly needed any sleep at all, which sounds nice, but it was just nonstop activity. I was getting so much done, or at least I thought I was. 

And then... when I started coming down from all that energy, I still wasn't quite back to being my normal self. That's when things started getting harder, with the sitting around and the cold coffee. I really try not to let it get that bad, I promise. I hope it's okay that it kind of went back and forth like that? I'm trying my best to explain it right for you.
During those times when you were so wound up and didn't need much sleep, was that energy so intense that it caused you to do things that were reckless or out of character for you?

Oh, um... reckless? No, no, I wouldn't say reckless. I really pride myself on being responsible, especially because of my work. I would never want to do anything that would put anyone at risk or make me look unprofessional. 

I mean, maybe I was just... very enthusiastic? I was starting a lot of new projects and talking to a lot of people, but I don't think I did anything bad or dangerous. I just had so much to give, you know? I was just trying to be productive. 

I might have spent a little more money than usual on art supplies for my painting, but... that's just a hobby, right? It's good to have hobbies. I really try to be careful with things like that. I hope that doesn't sound too out of character? I just want you to know I always try to do the right thing.
During those nine months, did the times when you felt very energetic and didn't need much sleep happen at the same time that you were hearing those voices and feeling like people were watching you?

Oh, um... yes, they did happen at the same time. I hope that's the right answer, I'm just trying to remember it all clearly for you. 

When I was in that phase where I was only sleeping a few hours a night and working on all those big plans for my art and my clients... that's when it was happening. I was in my little studio space, trying to get all my ideas out, and... well, that's when I would hear the voices the most. And that's also when I felt so sure that those other people were watching me and trying to take my work. 

I know it sounds like a lot to be dealing with all at once, and I really don't want you to think I was out of control or anything. I was still trying to keep everything together. Is it normal for all of that to happen at the same time? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
